races.name: Commonwealth Cup (Group 1) (No Geldings)

runners_data.name: Albert Einstein
runners_data.note: Three-year-old Aidan O'Brien colt who has won twice at 6f on Good and finished second at Group level — strong form credentials, but with so many prominent horses in this field he is unlikely to get the forward berth he wants and may find himself racing in a more restrained position than suits.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: James Owen's filly carries a headgear flag and has run nine times on Good or Firm ground with no wins — the step up to Group 1 level looks demanding, and she is a horse who naturally wants to race forward but will find that position occupied by classier rivals in this renewal.

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: Tony O'Brien's colt has been consistently placed without winning, finishing second three times including at Group level — wears tongue-tie, and while his prominent racing style is genuine, the congestion of pace in this field means he will likely be further back than he wants and his two-year-old form at the trip needs reproducing.

runners_data.name: Charles Darwin
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three on Good to Firm before a below-par run last time, the blinkers will sharpen his focus and he has the class and connections (O'Brien/Lordan) to take up a prominent berth — three wins at 5-6f on Good ground make him tailor-made for this surface and a fast-run race.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's colt has won twice at this exact 6f/Good to Firm combination and returned to winning ways last time — 49 days off is a minor query, but his consistency at the trip and course-type make him a natural fit for a race where holding prominent position early is currency.

runners_data.name: Division
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained with James Doyle aboard, this colt has won twice at 6f including on Good going — his last two runs were placed rather than winning but his style is well-suited to sitting just off Venetian Sun and he handles the surface well.

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has five runs at 5-6f on Good ground producing two wins — her natural inclination is to race forward, but with so many rivals wanting the same position in a 22-runner field, she may find herself shuffled back further than ideal and her OR of 101 looks the ceiling here.

runners_data.name: My Calyx Cen
runners_data.note: The French raider trained by Patrik Olave Valdivielso has won three on the spin including at 6f on Good at Goodwood — a light race record of just five runs makes him difficult to assess, and though he wants to race prominently, he may not command the front position his trainer would prefer in this size of field.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's colt who won at 6f and 7f on Good before struggling in handicap company — 83 days off is the longest break in the field, and while he has the ability to sit prominent, two consecutive defeats suggest he is currently below the form that would make him competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Outfielder
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's transatlantic raider is one of the few genuine hold-up horses, wearing a hood, with two starts in Britain showing fourth at Goodwood — American dirt form doesn't fully translate, and without solid turf evidence on Good to Firm he remains a speculative interest from the back.

runners_data.name: Rock On Thunder
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's colt wears a hood and prefers to be covered up — two recent sixth-place finishes and a tendency to race from rear means he needs the pace to collapse to get involved, which in a Venetian Sun-led race looks an unlikely outcome.

runners_data.name: Samangan
runners_data.note: F-H Graffard's colt has won three on the soft/heavy and was placed at 7f on soft last time — the sharp step up to Group 1 on Good to Firm ground is a significant and genuine concern for a horse whose form profile is clearly skewed to softer conditions.

runners_data.name: Song Of The Clyde
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's second string has won three times at 6f on Good going including his most recent outing — 34 days since his last win is ideal freshness and his pattern of settling just off the pace before quickening suits a Venetian Sun-controlled tempo perfectly.

runners_data.name: Super Soldier
runners_data.note: K R Burke's colt was out just six days ago and shows a string of poor finishes including 10th and 11th — on current form and fitness profile he looks outclassed at Group 1 level regardless of race shape, and a true hold-up style means he relies on an unlikely late collapse.

runners_data.name: Wise Approach
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick — a formidable combination — and this colt has form figures of 3W on all eight Good-ground starts, including wins at this trip and course type. Placed last twice but clearly at home on this surface and likely to be right in the mix from a forward position.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has won twice at 6f on Good and placed at 7f — she will look to race prominently by instinct, but the sheer depth of horses wanting that berth in this 22-runner field means she may be displaced from her preferred pitch, which would reduce her effectiveness materially.

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly returned to winning form last time at 6f on Good, and her record of three wins on Good ground is a strong asset — Gavin Ryan is an underrated jockey, and she is well-drawn for a prominent pitch; her form at 5-6f suits a fast-run 6f perfectly.

runners_data.name: Kimi Rey
runners_data.note: Graffard's second runner has placed on Good but her best form comes on heavy/soft at Longchamp — on Good to Firm at Ascot she has limited evidence to support a claim, and though she is a natural front-runner type, she will not command that position when facing this quality of field.

runners_data.name: Midnight Tango
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly (125lbs, females' weight) ran second last time at 6f on Good having been well beaten in three prior tries at 7f-8f — the drop back to 6f clearly sparked an improved effort and she is the most interesting of the hold-up horses if the race develops any chaos or compression.

runners_data.name: Spicy Marg
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly won at 6f on Good and has a broad range of going experience — her natural instinct is to get prominent but in a 22-runner field she is likely to be among those covered up in midfield, racing a position or two back from where she'd ideally be.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sun
runners_data.note: K R Burke's OR-115 top-weight is the only confirmed front-runner and has won four of her last seven starts including on Good and Soft going — Clifford Lee will bowl her to the front unchallenged, and her ability to control the fractions without being pressed gives her a tactical advantage no other runner in this field can replicate.

runners_data.name: Zanthos
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on the Simon & Ed Crisford-trained colt who has won at 7f on Good and been placed in Group company — his last run was a beaten ninth but all his best form is at 7f+, making the step back to a straight 6f a legitimate trip concern on Good to Firm ground.

races.paceDynamic: Venetian Sun is the confirmed lone front-runner in a 22-runner Group 1, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is set to bowl along in front at a controlled, self-managed tempo over Ascot's straight six furlongs on Good to Firm ground. Charles Darwin, Coppull, Division, Wise Approach, Samangan, Havana Anna, Song Of The Clyde and Zanthos all have prominent credentials and will track closely behind, creating a compact, fast-moving group from the off rather than a flat-out burn. The field contains markedly more prominent and front-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Albert Einstein, My Calyx Cen, Aspect Island, Brussels, Northern Champion, Kimi Rey, Spicy Marg, Fitzella and Havana Hurricane are all genuine prominent horses who have been pushed into midfield roles by the sheer volume of pace, with Charles Darwin, Coppull and Wise Approach the most likely to actually secure early position given class, draw and jockey quality. With Venetian Sun controlling a sustainable tempo unchallenged, and a dense pack of genuine prominents racing just off her, the profile that benefits most is the close-tracking prominent racer who can sit just off the pace, travel well, and quicken from two furlongs out — true hold-up horses face a stern test of finishing pace and must produce something exceptional to peg back horses who have travelled into the race from a forward position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Venetian Sun Leads, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Sun dictates a controlled pace and the prominent chasers — Charles Darwin, Wise Approach, Coppull — travel powerfully into the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Venetian Sun dictates a controlled pace and the prominent chasers — Charles Darwin, Wise Approach, Coppull — travel powerfully into the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed pack of redistributed prominent horses causes interference and traffic issues in the early and middle stages, slowing the effective tempo sufficiently to let hold-up horses close.
scenarios.body: If the compressed pack of redistributed prominent horses causes interference and traffic issues in the early and middle stages, slowing the effective tempo sufficiently to let hold-up horses close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Venetian Sun Front-Runs To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Sun's uncontested lead allows her to find an uninterrupted rhythm and she simply outstays the pursuers who fail to reel her in.
scenarios.body: If Venetian Sun's uncontested lead allows her to find an uninterrupted rhythm and she simply outstays the pursuers who fail to reel her in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Disrupts Tactics
scenarios.trigger: If high-drawn runners lose ground crossing to the rail or traffic prevents natural positions from being achieved in the first furlong of this straight six.
scenarios.body: If high-drawn runners lose ground crossing to the rail or traffic prevents natural positions from being achieved in the first furlong of this straight six.

watchPoints.text: Venetian Sun (K R Burke / Clifford Lee) goes unchallenged to the front in a 22-runner field — if she controls fractions below her sectional comfort zone, she may simply never be caught; watch whether any prominent horse is quick enough from the gate to pressure her early.

Charles Darwin and Wise Approach are the two highest-quality horses with both the ability and natural style to track Venetian Sun from prominent positions — if both travel powerfully into the final two furlongs, the race is likely decided between these three runners.

With nine-plus horses all naturally wanting to race prominently, the first two furlongs of this straight six could see significant shuffling and crowding as Albert Einstein, My Calyx Cen, Aspect Island and Brussels fail to find their preferred spots — watch for traffic casualties in the early stages.
Samangan's winning form is entirely on soft or heavy ground

races.name: Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a solid recent placed record over staying trips, including a second over 14f on good going 83 days ago; Luke Morris and James Owen are a low-profile combination but the horse's sim-going record over 10/15 hints at class for trip.

runners_data.name: Ambiente Friendly
runners_data.note: James Owen's second string, returning after a 307-day absence with a hood on — that layoff is a major flag, and while the 2-mile form at Ascot is strong, 19 rivals on a first run back makes this a harder task than the OR suggests.

runners_data.name: Mondo Man
runners_data.note: 75-day absence (407 days between runs prior to that) and a prominent style that suits this type of race, but sim-going figures are thin; Christophe Soumillon is a significant jockey booking and the trainer combination has decent recent form.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, clearly the pace anchor of the race; Gosden/Buick is a formidable combination, and the horse's recent form (1231-1) is strong, but he steps up markedly in trip from his last win at 10f, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing out of his usual role at this distance.

runners_data.name: Emit
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount from the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard, which is in good form at 8/55 over 14 days; the horse has been competitive in similar conditions and distance, and a prominent position just off the pace suits his profile well here.

runners_data.name: Plage De Havre
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is firing at 16/72, Oisin Murphy takes the ride, and the horse has a recent Goodwood win over 12f on good — going up in trip to 14f on this ground looks a logical progression rather than a stretch.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: Six of seven recent runs on good ground and three placed efforts in that sample, but none on a flat, galloping track like Ascot; Sean Levey rides for Hannon and the horse has been consistent without threatening to win.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: Two wins from seven on good ground and Jamie Spencer — a jockey renowned for finding gaps and timing runs — adds tactical interest; the yard has minimal recent form but the horse's 12f win on good last time out is directly relevant.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: True prominent type who has won over 12f on good, but the last two runs (9th and 8th) show form trailing off; McMonagle rides for O'Brien and a step back to a more conventional pace scenario might help him settle.

runners_data.name: Hopewell Rock
runners_data.note: James Doyle for George Boughey, a combination worth noting given the trainer's recent quieter spell; placed on good ground at this trip last time out, and his profile as a consistent stayer suits a race run at a moderate clip.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: William Haggas's runner with James McDonald aboard — a top combination — and the horse has two wins at 11-12f on good; a natural prominent type who has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the front, meaning he may be unable to express his best running style.

runners_data.name: Military Academy
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning in this company, the blinkers (hg:b) are now well-established gear and his record on good going is modest; Billy Loughnane rides and the horse has been placed only once in the last five runs.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: A 96-day break and a patchy record — including a 20th at Haydock and a 16th at Haydock — offset by a win at 8f on soft; 14f on good-to-firm at Ascot stretches this horse's comfort zone on multiple fronts.

runners_data.name: Insanity
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan rides this Alan King runner who has an excellent placed record (3 wins, 8 places from 15 sim-going runs) and strong form at 10-12f on good; by nature a front-runner who will find himself further back than ideal in this crowded field, which blunts his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Six wins from 15 career starts on good ground underlines the ability, and Colin Keane is an excellent booking, but 120 days off and a horse who naturally wants to be prominent in a race where the front is already crowded creates a real tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: Three consecutive 7ths after winning twice, and the sim-going record (5/8, 2W2P) shows the ground is fine; Neil Callan rides and the horse has the ability to compete but his form line has deteriorated noticeably since his wins.

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: Five of his last five runs have been on standard ground at Ascot and none on turf with good going — all five were on Tapeta — which makes his turf figures essentially unknown and the going suitability a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Regal Ulixes
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's second runner via PJ McDonald; won at 10f on standard but his turf record on good is light, and as a redistributed prominent type he too may find himself unable to get into his preferred forward position in this large field.

runners_data.name: Serengeti
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark rides this lightly-raced Mike Murphy runner who won at 10f on good last time (25 days ago); a true hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to the density at the rear, and the step up to 14f at this level is a significant ask.

races.paceDynamic: Warrant Holder is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Ascot, and with William Buick aboard he will control tempo from the outset without any credible challenger likely to press him into a battle. The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 1m4f trip, which rewards horses who travel fluently and finish strongly rather than those who grind. Several horses tagged as prominent — Opportunity, Insanity, Dain Ma Nut In, and Regal Ulixes — are true front-running or prominent types who cannot all find their natural berth in this shape, meaning Warrant Holder's lead is essentially uncontested and the pace will be measured rather than pressured. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate at the front, and among those most likely to actually secure a forward position behind Warrant Holder are Emit, Plage De Havre, and French Duke, given recent form, trainer momentum, and jockey profile. This race shape — a lone, unchallenged leader setting a sustainable gallop — strongly favours closers with a clean, efficient turn of foot who can pick off a field strung out over the final two furlongs, particularly hold-up types with good recent form on similar going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Warrant Holder Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Warrant Holder bowls along in front at a fair but unhurried pace and the prominent pack settles without challenging him, setting up a straight-line test of finishing quality.
scenarios.body: If Warrant Holder bowls along in front at a fair but unhurried pace and the prominent pack settles without challenging him, setting up a straight-line test of finishing quality.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that the hold-up brigade get a strong tow into the race and have enough time and room to unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that the hold-up brigade get a strong tow into the race and have enough time and room to unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Gang Up
scenarios.trigger: If Emit, Plage De Havre, and Hopewell Rock push forward to track Warrant Holder closely, injecting enough pressure to string the field out and set up a race for those with tactical versatility.
scenarios.body: If Emit, Plage De Havre, and Hopewell Rock push forward to track Warrant Holder closely, injecting enough pressure to string the field out and set up a race for those with tactical versatility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In A Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field produces significant traffic issues, forcing mid-race positional reshuffling that catches several fancied horses in the wrong place at the wrong turn.
scenarios.body: If the large 19-runner field produces significant traffic issues, forcing mid-race positional reshuffling that catches several fancied horses in the wrong place at the wrong turn.

watchPoints.text: Warrant Holder's unchallenged lead is the single biggest tactical factor — if Buick softens the pace through the first mile at Good to Firm, he sets up a sprint finish that could allow the prominent horses camping just behind him (Emit, Plage De Havre) to time their run perfectly.

Opportunity, Insanity, and Dain Ma Nut In are all natural prominent types who cannot be in their preferred position — watch for any of them becoming trapped in traffic on the final turn, especially in a 19-runner field where the straight at Ascot can bottle up horses wide of the rail.

The large field (19 runners) over 1m4f at Ascot means the early stages through the back straight will be congested — hold-up horses like Burdett Road and Ambiente Friendly need a clean passage turning for home or their finishing kick will be irrelevant.

Ambiente Friendly returns from 307 days off with a hood — a combination of a long break and a big field on fast ground creates a material risk of the horse needing the run, and Cieren Fallon will be managing that uncertainty throughout.

Teumessias Fox has run all five recent starts on Tapeta at Ascot — his turf form on good ground is essentially a blank, and punters should treat any market move with real caution given the surface switch is completely unexplored in his recent history.

races.name: Coronation Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Balantina
runners_data.note: Won on the all-weather at Dundalk last time, but her best turf form includes a win at Royal Ascot last year and strong placed efforts on good ground — the step back to a mile suits, and Oisin Murphy riding for the Aidan O'Brien satellite operation adds confidence; a natural prominent runner who should get her position comfortably here.

runners_data.name: Black Caviar Gold
runners_data.note: Went in twice on soft ground earlier in the season but has finished fourth twice on good — the step up to a mile is unproven and while she is a natural front-runner at heart, she faces too many speed rivals here and will likely find herself racing in an unnatural midfield position that blunts her effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Moon Target
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly returns after 252 days off, a significant fitness query for a Group 1; she is a genuine prominent racer by inclination but with six other pace-biased rivals in the field, she is unlikely to secure the forward berth she needs, making her chance heavily dependent on settling for an unfamiliar hold-up role.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien on the highest-rated returning three-year-old filly in the field — five wins from seven starts on good ground and a prominent racing style that maps perfectly to this race shape make her the standout on paper; the one blot was a seventh at Epsom on good, but otherwise her record is exemplary.

runners_data.name: Rose Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' filly won on soft and has two form figures of 10 and 6 on good ground, raising a genuine surface concern on today's going; she is a prominent type by nature but is being mapped to midfield under pressure from pace rivals, and her limited exposure to conditions like today is a material risk.

runners_data.name: Sukanya
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up horse in the field — Tom Marquand will ride patiently and she will need a strong pace to close into; she won impressively on good ground at Windsor last time over seven furlongs, and the step to a mile looks a positive step for her stamina-based profile, but she is reliant on the tempo being strong enough.

runners_data.name: Timeforshowcasing
runners_data.note: Won at Lingfield on standard and has a win on soft but only three runs on good ground with mixed results — a natural front-runner who Billy Loughnane may attempt to push forward, but the presence of True Love means she is likely to be shuffled back from her preferred lead position, which is a real structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Touleen
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' filly has strong form on good ground over seven furlongs, including two wins and a placed effort in her last five runs at that trip — stepping up to a mile on Good to Firm looks an interesting stamina test and Saffie Osborne rides for a trainer in fine form (3/8 in 14 days); she is a genuine prominent type who should get a clean run in second or third.

runners_data.name: True Love
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner and winner of five of her last nine starts on fast ground — she should lead without serious challenge and the question is whether her controlled gallop sets it up for herself or for the closers behind her; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that if she is caught up in a contested pace she may not see it out, but on current evidence she gets a soft lead.

races.paceDynamic: True Love is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to contest the lead, she should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down Ascot's straight mile on Good to Firm ground. The pace she sets is likely to be honest but controlled — enough to test stamina without inviting a sprint finish, creating a race that rewards horses who can track close to her and sustain their effort into the final furlong. Four horses — Timeforshowcasing, Moon Target, Black Caviar Gold and Rose Ghaiyyath — are natural prominent racers who have been pushed into midfield on the map because there are simply more speed-biased types than the race shape can accommodate; of those, Timeforshowcasing and Black Caviar Gold are most likely to push forward and apply some pressure, though they will need to overcome their out-of-role positioning. The dominant tactical verdict is clear: horses who can sit prominently just behind True Love and quicken off a genuine but unexaggerated pace are most favoured — meaning genuine prominent-to-midfield types with a clean turn of foot on quick ground hold the decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: True Love Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If True Love leads without serious pressure and sets a fair, controlled tempo that suits a sustained finishing effort.
scenarios.body: If True Love leads without serious pressure and sets a fair, controlled tempo that suits a sustained finishing effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracking Pair Outstay Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough that the closers lack a true target and the prominent stalkers grind out a staying advantage in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just steady enough that the closers lack a true target and the prominent stalkers grind out a staying advantage in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If True Love or a displaced prominent type burns energy in a faster-than-expected first half, leaving the race open for a hold-up finisher.
scenarios.body: If True Love or a displaced prominent type burns energy in a faster-than-expected first half, leaving the race open for a hold-up finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Helps Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If a confused early pace — caused by multiple redirected prominent types pushing forward simultaneously — leads to an erratic gallop and a muddling finish.
scenarios.body: If a confused early pace — caused by multiple redirected prominent types pushing forward simultaneously — leads to an erratic gallop and a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Precise for Ryan Moore — if she travels smoothly in the prominent berth just behind True Love, her record of five wins on good ground and dominant form profile makes her the one most likely to account for any pace advantage True Love creates.

True Love's lead may not be as uncontested as it appears — Timeforshowcasing and Black Caviar Gold are both natural front-runners being mapped back against their will, and if either pushes forward aggressively in the first furlong, the tempo could jump sharply and compromise True Love's stamina reserves.

Balantina returns after 231 days off the track — her Dundalk win came on the all-weather and her last turf run was several months ago; watch how she moves to post and how she handles the quicker ground after a lengthy absence.

Sukanya is the only true hold-up horse in the race — if the early sectionals are genuinely strong (driven by displaced prominent types pushing up), she becomes significantly more interesting; if the pace is merely moderate, her chance diminishes sharply regardless of her finishing kick.

Moon Target's 252-day absence from competition is the longest layoff in the field for a Group 1 — Sir Mark Prescott is adept at preparing horses for a reappearance, but the combination of fitness uncertainty, an out-of-role positional problem, and mixed going form on today's surface makes her a high-risk proposition.

races.name: Sandringham Stakes (Handicap) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Billy Loughnane takes the initiative from stall one and an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground suits her best, though she has not won since June last year and her OR=101 marks this as a career-high assignment — style fit is strong but class ceiling is the query.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides and Andrew Balding sends her here on the back of a solid campaign at seven and eight furlongs; five-from-five on Good ground in similar conditions is a compelling statistic, and a prominent position directly behind Awaken looks within reach for a horse of this profile.

runners_data.name: Hope Queen
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts and both on Good ground at seven to eight furlongs for K R Burke — she is lightly raced but progressing steeply, and Clifford Lee can sit her prominently where the race is won from in this shape.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Angel
runners_data.note: Three wins in the book including two at eight furlongs on Good ground and Robert Havlin knows the horse; she has been off 27 days, has the form to be top-four in the weights, and her prominent style puts her ideally in the firing line for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Spinning Lizzie
runners_data.note: Won over eight furlongs at Standard, third over ten furlongs most recently — stepping back in trip is fine but the ten-furlong run on Good suggests she may want a stronger pace than Awaken will provide; Rossa Ryan holds the booking.

runners_data.name: Zooming
runners_data.note: Won at seven furlongs on Soft and placed on Good, but her last run at six furlongs on Good was a modest seventh — William Haggas sends her back up to a mile and Tom Marquand rides, though she has not won on Good to Firm and her form line is less compelling than several rivals.

runners_data.name: Seet
runners_data.note: Won her last two including an eight-furlong handicap on Good ground just 14 days ago — Ryan Moore takes the ride and the quick return under a penalty is a concern, but her form and jockey represent the most compelling combination of any horse in the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Al Rateel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just three starts and a style that is unclassified; Warren Fentiman claims three pounds and the French trainer has no recent Ascot form — too many unknowns to assess with confidence despite a fair handicap mark of 95.

runners_data.name: Repel
runners_data.note: Won at six furlongs on Good and placed at the same trip — Colin Keane is a significant jockey booking and F-H Graffard's horses travel well, but stepping up to a mile for the first time on Good to Firm for a trainer without UK course form is a question she needs to answer.

runners_data.name: Mixed Feelings
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking and she won over eight furlongs on Soft for Joseph O'Brien — but zero placed finishes on Good ground from three attempts is a real concern on today's surface, and her last run was a flat fifth over ten furlongs.

runners_data.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners_data.note: Won at six furlongs on Good and placed on Soft — Gary Carroll keeps the ride but she goes up in trip to a mile for the first time on Good to Firm ground, and a step in distance for a trainer with moderate Ascot strike rate adds risk.

runners_data.name: Glyfada
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts including over eight and ten furlongs on Good ground and she's trained by Donnacha O'Brien with Oisin Murphy taking the ride — this is one of the more interesting profiles in the race with upward form trajectory and genuine class.

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: A complicated form line — two placings at eight furlongs on Good but also a 13th and an 11th at this trip; William Buick is a strong booking but her inconsistency on Good ground makes her a difficult proposition despite the jockey confidence.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Breeze
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who won last time out over eight furlongs on Good ground for Jane Chapple-Hyam — David Egan rides and she is one of only two horses whose natural style suits the come-from-behind scenario, though this race shape may not produce a strong enough pace to bring her home.

runners_data.name: Brigid's Well
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has a win at eight furlongs on Good to her name and wears a tongue-tie, but as a natural prominent racer she is likely to find herself further back than ideal in this field, which dilutes her chance considerably given her preferred style demands a forward berth.

runners_data.name: Blingy's Sister
runners_data.note: Won at six furlongs on Good and has solid placed form at the same trip — Toby Moore (7lb claimer) rides and she is another Hugo Palmer runner who will struggle to secure her natural prominent position given the volume of front-running types in this field; her best form is over shorter distances too.

runners_data.name: Tavana
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride and she won at seven furlongs on Soft for Ed Smyth-Osbourne — the trainer has no Ascot form, and while she is a genuine front-runner by inclination, the congestion in this field means she is likely to sit further back than ideal in a race where that costs ground.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Angel
runners_data.note: Alexandra Egan (7lb claim) partners this Jane Chapple-Hyam-trained filly who has two wins at seven furlongs on Good — she is a natural racer from the front but in a 30-runner field the position simply will not be available to her, and the apprentice claim may not compensate for running from an unsuitable slot.

runners_data.name: Bintaziza
runners_data.note: Unbeaten on Synthetic (two wins) but only a fourth on Good ground — Ray Dawson rides and Roger Varian has strong figures in the fortnight, but her best surface appears to be all-weather and her ability to reproduce that form on Good to Firm turf is unproven; she will be running from a position further back than she prefers.

runners_data.name: Green Carrera
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground at eight furlongs for Joseph O'Brien and Mickael Barzalona is an elite booking — she wears a tongue-tie and her form at a mile on Good is genuinely strong, though she too will be squeezed into midfield against her natural instincts.

runners_data.name: She Commands
runners_data.note: Jack Dace (5lb claim) rides this Ralph Beckett-trained filly who has won at eight furlongs twice, both on Synthetic — her only Turf run was a fifth on Soft and she has never raced on Good to Firm, so the surface query is significant even if she is mapped at the rear simply because the field is short on true hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Gallop
runners_data.note: Three wins in her career including at eight furlongs on Good ground, and Aurelien Lemaitre is an accomplished booking — she has been off 47 days, is a natural prominent type who will be pushed back by weight of numbers, and a flat seventeenth on Good last time suggests she is not in the form of her winning runs.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Majesty
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides for John and Thady Gosden who have strong recent figures — she has won at eight furlongs on Good but her only run on Synthetic was a fifth, and she ends up shown at the rear not by inclination but because she is among the least pace-committed midfielders in a field that has too many similar types.

runners_data.name: Lyrics Of Life
runners_data.note: One of only two genuinely natural hold-up performers in the field alongside Harlequin Breeze — Silvestre De Sousa has ridden her consistently and she has four places from five runs on Good ground, but her lack of a win from fourteen career starts is a nagging concern even if the race shape one day aligns in her favour.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Won at seven furlongs on Good for Ed Walker — Luke Morris rides and she has been off 54 days, which is a notable gap, but her recent win and Good-ground form suggest she merits respect; as a natural prominent racer she will be forced back by this field's composition and that is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Rosa Inglesa
runners_data.note: Won at eight furlongs on Soft and placed on Good — Harry Davies rides for Charlie Fellowes, she has been off 31 days, and her placed form at seven furlongs on Good is workmanlike; like several in this group she is a prominent runner who will not get that position today.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners this Donnacha

races.paceDynamic: Awaken is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 30-runner field and, with no genuine pressure expected, she should dictate a controlled, honest gallop around Ascot's round mile on Good to Firm ground — sustainable rather than scorching. The mass of prominent-style horses beneath her (Mubasimah, Hope Queen, Just Call Me Angel, Seet, Spinning Lizzie, Zooming, Repel and others) will compress into a tight pack immediately behind, creating a bunched, convoy-style race through the first half with relatively even tempo. The field holds far more genuine prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate: Brigid's Well, Blingy's Sister, Tavana, Harlequin Angel, Bintaziza, Green Carrera and others are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be squeezed into midfield positions they are not accustomed to, with Mubasimah, Hope Queen, Just Call Me Angel and Seet — better-credentialled and better-jockeyed — most likely to actually secure the positions immediately behind Awaken. With a steady pace and a large field fanning wide turning for home, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in the first five or six, travel without cover and quicken; genuine hold-up horses face the compound problem of a moderate tempo and traffic in a 30-runner handicap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Awaken sets a controlled pace and the prominent horses immediately behind her travel comfortably to the two-furlong pole before unleashing their finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: If Awaken sets a controlled pace and the prominent horses immediately behind her travel comfortably to the two-furlong pole before unleashing their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class kicks clear turning in
scenarios.trigger: If the race quickens sharply entering the straight and the higher-rated prominent horses use superior quality to put the race to bed before the lower-weighted closers can organise.
scenarios.body: If the race quickens sharply entering the straight and the higher-rated prominent horses use superior quality to put the race to bed before the lower-weighted closers can organise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late movers thread through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough — or the field fans wide enough in the straight — to create a passage for the genuine hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough — or the field fans wide enough in the straight — to create a passage for the genuine hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front runner stays clear
scenarios.trigger: If Awaken's uncontested lead allows her to bowl along at her own pace and the prominent pack behind fail to reel her in before the line.
scenarios.body: If Awaken's uncontested lead allows her to bowl along at her own pace and the prominent pack behind fail to reel her in before the line.

races.name: King Edward VII Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)

runners_data.name: Ancient Egypt
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's colt finished 8th over 12f on Soft then bounced back to win twice over a mile on Good ground, suggesting the step back to 1m4f suits but this surface is a key positive; naturally a prominent racer, he is shown at the rear purely because every other runner in this small field also wants to race up with the pace, and his 13-day turnaround is brisk but Johnston runs horses fit.

runners_data.name: Causeway
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, Ryan Moore takes over from the rider who won aboard last time, and the O'Brien colt arrives on the back of three consecutive wins culminating in a 10f victory on Good — only 2 of his 5 career runs have come on similar ground but both were winning efforts; uncontested in front, he is the pivotal horse in how this race is run.

runners_data.name: Echo Of Stars
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's lightly-raced three-year-old is a genuine 10f performer on Good ground, winning at Nottingham last time over this exact trip before a Group-class outing at Chester; his style is front-running by inclination but the density of prominent types in this race has pushed his mapping rearward — he carries headgear (t) and Spencer's patient hold-up reputation may actually fit the reshuffled position better than most redistributed horses here.

runners_data.name: Golden Story
runners_data.note: Burke's colt arrives on the back of a hat-trick including a win over 11f on Good, making him a solid stayer on this surface, and Clifford Lee has ridden him in both recent wins; his natural desire to race prominently cannot be satisfied in this shape with Causeway dominating, and his chance hinges on whether the pace is strong enough to bring his stamina into play in the straight.

runners_data.name: Venetian Prince
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt won over 11f on Heavy at Chelmsford before a string of placed efforts and a 10th on Good at Epsom — the Ascot straight mile-and-a-half is a fresh test, but his stamina credentials are sound and Watson's booking suggests this is a serious entry; of the prominent types, he appears most likely to genuinely press Causeway given his willingness to race up with the pace and his positive return to winning form last time.

runners_data.name: Water To Wine
runners_data.note: Gosden and Buick's unbeaten two-from-two colt is the most progressive unknown in the race, having won both starts over 11f on Good at Sandown and Goodwood; his instinct is to race prominently but with Causeway firmly in control of the pace he is unlikely to secure that role — the key question is whether Buick can find a position close enough to the action to deploy his finishing kick when it matters.

races.paceDynamic: Causeway, trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Ryan Moore, is the one confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just six where every other runner carries a prominent tag, he is highly likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, uncontested tempo over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Ascot. With no genuine hold-up horse in the field and multiple prominent types — Water To Wine, Golden Story, Echo Of Stars, and Ancient Egypt — unable to secure their natural position, the pace is unlikely to be pressured and Causeway can set a measured, confidence-building gallop that suits a horse who quickens from the front. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than this race shape can accommodate, and of those, Causeway and Venetian Prince are best placed to actually secure their preferred position, with Water To Wine (Buick, Gosden) and Golden Story the most likely to push forward for a share of the early ground. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-tracking profile: a controlled pace with a single injection of pace in the final two furlongs will suit those who travel well close to the action rather than those trying to make ground from an unnatural rear position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Causeway Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Causeway sets an uncontested, honest gallop and Ryan Moore delivers the decisive move turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Causeway sets an uncontested, honest gallop and Ryan Moore delivers the decisive move turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Prince or Golden Story pressures Causeway sufficiently to force a genuine pace contest throughout.
scenarios.body: If Venetian Prince or Golden Story pressures Causeway sufficiently to force a genuine pace contest throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Burst From The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow early that the race degenerates into a sprint finish, giving those held wider in midfield a sprint-style opportunity.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so slow early that the race degenerates into a sprint finish, giving those held wider in midfield a sprint-style opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a stumble or interference disrupts Causeway's lead and the race fragments into individual efforts without a settled front-runner.
scenarios.body: If a stumble or interference disrupts Causeway's lead and the race fragments into individual efforts without a settled front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Causeway — if Ryan Moore jumps him smartly from a handy draw and immediately takes up the running uncontested, the race shape is set in stone from the first furlong and every other scenario becomes significantly less likely.

Water To Wine and Golden Story — watch whether Buick or Lee attempt to push their horses up to challenge Causeway early; any early pressure on the leader dramatically changes the pace dynamic and opens the race up for stamina-based runners.

Venetian Prince — his 10th of 10 at Epsom last time was a significant form blip on Good ground; if he again fails to travel on this surface, it removes the one runner most likely to set up an honest gallop by pressing Causeway.

Echo Of Stars — Jamie Spencer's record of riding hold-up races should be monitored; if Spencer drops him in early having been mapped to midfield, it is a positive tell that the horse is comfortable in the revised role rather than fighting for a position he cannot get.

Ancient Egypt — at 13 days since his last run, watch his pre-race behaviour in the paddock; a quick turnaround is not unusual for Johnston but any sign of tension or sweat would be relevant given he is already racing out of his most comfortable positional role.

races.name: Palace Of Holyroodhouse (Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dickensian
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race; Shane Gray has just this horse to aim at clear air on good to firm ground he handles in every run, and at OR 104 he is at the top of his mark, but dictating from the front suits him perfectly and Kevin Ryan's yard has been in strong form (3 wins from 29, 14 days).

runners_data.name: Moojeed
runners_data.note: Barzalona rides for the classy Graffard yard but Moojeed's best form has come on soft ground (two wins in softer conditions) and his recent runs on good going (3rd, 5th) suggest the quick Ascot surface may blunt his effectiveness today.

runners_data.name: Revival Power
runners_data.note: A genuine 5f specialist with three wins from seven outings at this trip on good ground; Tim Easterby's yard has been busy (7/98, 14 days) and David Allan knows the horse well, though a mark of OR 102 asks questions after his latest 7th.

runners_data.name: Ten Carat Harry
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 6f at Royal Ascot suggesting he handles the track, but his best trip may be beyond 5f and his form over the minimum trip is limited; William Carver takes the ride on a horse whose last two wins came at 6f and 7f.

runners_data.name: Sirius A
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes this for the lightly-raced James Horton, and Sirius A's last win came on standard going at 6f — the drop to 5f and switch to Ascot turf is untested, but his OR 100 and elite booking make him a fascinating watch early on.

runners_data.name: Bacio
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's two-year-old arrives from America with a strong speed profile (sole UK run was 2nd on firm ground at 5f) and at OR 100 with Juan Hernandez aboard, his raw pace is clearly respected — the big question is whether international travel and an open-field Ascot handicap suit a juvenile.

runners_data.name: Sandal's Song
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes the ride on a George Weaver-trained American import who has won on firm and placed on good at 5f; the combination of a top jockey and course-specific experience over the trip makes this a credible each-way angle at OR 99.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: The Balding-McMonagle combination is worth noting, but Ghost Mode's two most recent runs returned 9th and 7th on good ground; his wins came at 6-7f on softer surfaces and a drop to 5f Ascot handicap looks a tricky assignment for his current form.

runners_data.name: Comical Point
runners_data.note: William Buick rides for the same Balding yard (12/57 recently) and Comical Point has posted consistent form figures with four placings in his last five, all on good or soft at 6f — the drop to a sharp 5f represents a slightly unexplored dimension.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: Has been off 95 days which demands respect in a tight 5f handicap; best form came at 5f on standard-to-slow going and his runs on good ground have been mixed, so the layoff and ground may combine against him today.

runners_data.name: Simplify
runners_data.note: Three wins from seven at 5-6f on good or good-to-soft ground, and Balding's stable is striking at 12/57 in 14 days — McDonald's experience over a trip where this horse clearly excels makes Simplify one of the most convincing pace-to-finish profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: May Angel
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up runner alongside Zelaina in a field that is otherwise almost entirely pace-dominated; Oisin Murphy takes the ride but May Angel's best form has been at 7f, and a compact 5f Ascot sprint with no real gap to close into is a notably different test.

runners_data.name: Jazl
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 6f on good ground show a horse hitting form, but Simon & Ed Crisford's runner is a natural front-runner whose position has been redistributed rearward by the volume of pace in this field — his true role is prominent and he is likely to push forward regardless of the map position.

runners_data.name: Westport
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts (5f, 6f, 6f on good and standard), Boughey's three-year-old has won every time he has run and Loughnane rides; also a natural front-runner squeezed by the redistribution, expect Westport to attempt to push up early and his unbeaten profile makes him highly relevant.

runners_data.name: Gentle George
runners_data.note: Wins at 5f on soft and 6f conditions suggest he handles give in the ground better than fast ground; his prominent style has been displaced to midfield by the sheer volume of pace runners, and on good to firm his form record here (0/3 on similar going) is a concern.

runners_data.name: Exclamation
runners_data.note: OR 94 and a big-field handicap type who has shown flashes (one win at 5f on good ground) but also a string of 9th and 14th finishes; Ashley Lewis (5) takes the ride and his true prominent style will see him bidding to go forward, but the weight of evidence suggests this is a competitive ask.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on standard going and recently placed at 4th on good; David Egan rides a horse who naturally wants to race prominently and will try to get forward despite being shown in midfield — her form at the trip is better than her current OR 94 suggests.

runners_data.name: Gold Digger
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts at 6f on good ground (OR 94) makes Gold Digger a progressive and lightly-raced filly; Saffie Osborne takes the ride and while her natural style is prominent rather than mid-pack, her recent record of 1-6-1 in three career starts on this surface demands attention.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Wins at 5f and 6f on good ground show course-and-trip form; Shoemark is a strong jockey booking for Ed Walker (7/37, 14 days) and Black Star Boy is a prominent racer who will push forward, though the redistribution reflects the overcrowded nature of the pace group today.

runners_data.name: Calico Blue
runners_data.note: Three wins from four starts at 5-6f including two on good ground; Varian's yard has been very active (11/35, 14 days) and Ray Dawson takes the ride — his form profile is strong but the 56-day break is the one flag, and his natural prominent style is squeezed by the field's makeup.

runners_data.name: Miss Yechance
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good ground and placed twice over 6f at the same going, but the 105-day layoff is a significant concern in a big Ascot handicap; the Antonio Cintra & Julio Olascoaga yard has been quiet and De Sousa will have to produce a fresh horse from a cold preparation.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Three wins on good going over 5f from eight career starts gives Dazzling Haze a strong pace profile for this trip; Marquand rides and his OR 91 potentially underestimates him in a field where so many are racing out of their natural position — a genuine 5f performer on this going.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Spell
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good and twice at 6f (good and standard) making her unexpectedly potent over this exact trip and surface; Kevin Philippart De Foy has had recent winners (1/17, 14 days) and Rowan Scott keeps the ride on a horse better than her OR 90 might suggest after a 48-day break.

runners_data.name: Tricky Tel
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back at 5f and 6f on good ground (OR 90) and ran only six days ago, which suggests he is bouncing; Toby Moore (7) claims 7lb and the Hugo Palmer yard (5/35, 14 days) is in form — the double penalty of short recovery and a big field makes his chance dependent on how he handles the hustle.

runners_data.name: Cherry Baker
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good and standard, and Cieren Fallon takes the ride for James Owen's yard which has been active (6/51, 14 days); his step back to OR 89

races.paceDynamic: Dickensian is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of 28 that is overwhelmingly packed with prominent-racing types, meaning he is highly likely to bowl along in front essentially uncontested on his own terms on good to firm ground over this straight five furlongs at Ascot. With no genuine rival willing or able to push him hard from the gates, the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, creating a true-run race without the suicidal fractions that would otherwise string the field out. Horses like Westport, Jazl, Sirius A, Simplify and Comical Point will all attempt to press up behind him, but the rail draw, jockey positioning and sheer volume of prominent types mean several will be shuffled wider or further back than their handlers intend. This race shape strongly favours confirmed prominent racers who can secure a forward berth early and travel into the race — pure hold-up horses are almost non-existent in this field, and the redistributed types mapped artificially to midfield or rear are not genuine closers, meaning a late sweeping finish is unlikely to materialise. The field contains far more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their natural position; Dickensian, Sirius A, Simplify and Westport are best-placed to secure the positions closest to the pace, with the likes of Gentle George, Ipanema Queen, Gold Digger and Exclamation likely to be denied their natural spots.

scenarios.title: Dickensian Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dickensian breaks cleanly and is allowed to control a steady-to-moderate gallop with no rival willing to commit to pressing him hard.
scenarios.body: If Dickensian breaks cleanly and is allowed to control a steady-to-moderate gallop with no rival willing to commit to pressing him hard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Edges Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leading prominent types breaks sharply and secures a coveted position just off Dickensian, then picks up neatly in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If one of the leading prominent types breaks sharply and secures a coveted position just off Dickensian, then picks up neatly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Bottleneck
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace causes a wall of horses to bunch in midfield and a gap opens late down the rail or up the far side for a horse who has been held up fractionally.
scenarios.body: If the moderate pace causes a wall of horses to bunch in midfield and a gap opens late down the rail or up the far side for a horse who has been held up fractionally.

scenarios.title: Draw And Pace Disadvantage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely falsely run and high-drawn horses fail to secure any position, allowing an unexpectedly prominent effort from a lower-rated type to steal it.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely falsely run and high-drawn horses fail to secure any position, allowing an unexpectedly prominent effort from a lower-rated type to steal it.
